title: Turn a single-player game into co-op with an agent
summary: A poster shares a repo whose instructions let Claude Code revive or build co-op mods for games; it lists Deus Ex as released and Ocarina of Time as fully synced.
agent_role: The agent researches existing mods or reverse engineers the game, adds networking and state syncing, runs tests with real game clients and opens a draft pull request; the human reviews it.
outcome: The post reports Deus Ex co-op released and Zelda: Ocarina of Time fully synced, with Fallout: New Vegas and others in progress.
what_they_did: A poster shared a repo with instructions for coding agents. You paste two lines naming a game. The agent either repairs a broken co-op mod or reverse engineers the game to add one. It then tests with real game clients and opens a draft change for review.
how_it_went: The post says Deus Ex co-op is released and Ocarina of Time is fully synced. Several other games and 230+ mods are listed as in progress or gaps.
worth_knowing: Some games take far more agent hours than others. The rules require owning the game, a copy per player, and no touching anti-cheat or others' online play.
prompt: Read https://github.com/cranebeaker/coop-anything and follow AGENTS.md. I want to play [game I own] in co-op with my friends. First check whether a co-op mod already exists and show me your plan. Only work with my legally owned copy and do not touch anti-cheat or online multiplayer. Wait for my approval before submitting any pull request.

curation.rationale: A novel workflow where agents research, reverse engineer and test co-op mods for games, with named results like Deus Ex; posted by a promoter rather than the repo creator, in a hype tone.
